description: OPLS/2020 analog types for atoms that no OPLS rule (SMARTS rules, atom-type archive) types and that therefore have a GAFF2 type (user decision 2026-10-29). An atom whose GAFF2 type is listed and that matches the SMARTS (atom mapped :1) takes the OPLS/2020 type: its class (bonded lookup) and Lennard-Jones; charges are CM1A either way. Each type is a representative of an OPLS/2020 class with the same element, hybridization and bond order; only such unambiguous analogs are listed. Not listed, so kept as GAFF2: C=S, C=N, N-N, N=N, N=O and N-O groups, sp/sp2 non-aromatic C other than C=O, 5-membered heteroaromatic rings, 3- and 4-membered rings, halogens on N/O/S/P/Si. Heavy-atom rules are applied first; rules with parent_typed apply to a hydrogen only if its heavy atom then has an OPLS type, so a group kept as GAFF2 keeps its hydrogens. First matching rule wins.

exclusions.why: An analog's class is looked up in the OPLS/2020 table first, so a wrong analog gives a plausible but wrong table term (e.g. CT-CT-CT ~112 deg for a 60 deg cyclopropane angle) instead of a miss, and nothing downstream catches it. The 2026-10-29 census found crude GAFF2->OPLS class mapping unsafe: ~50 deg angle errors in 3-rings, ~15 deg in 5-ring heteroaromatics, bond-order errors. An analog is listed only if the table's geometry stays valid for the atom; otherwise the atom keeps GAFF2 (gaff2.dat terms fitted for its chemistry, or the QM fit with --qm).
exclusions.3- and 4-membered rings: ring angles ~60/90 deg; every OPLS sp3 class encodes ~109-112 deg (sp3-C rules carry !r3;!r4). Epoxides use the real OPLS/2020 epoxide types via archive borrow rules.
exclusions.5-membered heteroaromatic rings: OPLS 5-ring classes (CW, CR, NA, NB, ...) are ring-specific with ~108 deg internal angles; a 6-ring analog (CA, NC) would take 120 deg terms (aromatic-C and azine-N rules carry !r5). Pyrazole/indazole use real types via borrow rules.
exclusions.C=S, C=N: the natural analogs (C=O, C=C) change the partner element or bond order, so b0, k and conjugation torsions would come from the wrong bond; C=N chemistry (imines, amidines, oximes, hydrazones) is too varied for one class.
exclusions.N-N, N=N, N=O, N-O: hydrazines, azo, nitroso, nitro, hydroxylamines, N-oxides: hybridization, lone-pair character and bond order differ from amine/amide N (nitro is delocalized and charge-separated); amine/amide rules carry !$(N-[N,O]).
exclusions.non-aromatic sp/sp2 C other than C=O: ordinary alkenes, alkynes and nitriles are already OPLS-typed; what is left (allenes, ketenes, C=N/C=S carbons, strongly conjugated C) has bond orders no single class fits.
exclusions.halogens on N/O/S/P/Si: OPLS halogen LJ and classes are fitted for C-X; N/O/S/P/Si-X bonds differ in polarity and length and the table has no bonded terms for them, so an analog would only change LJ (halogen-typing decision, 2026-10-29).

rules.name: sulfonyl-S
rules.note: S(=O)2 in sulfonic acids, sulfonates, sulfates, sulfonate esters, sulfonyl halides: sulfone S (SY).

rules.name: sulfoxide-S
rules.note: Sulfinyl S: sulfoxide S (SZ).

rules.name: sulfoxide-O
rules.note: O of a sulfinyl S: sulfoxide O (OY).

rules.name: sulfonyl-O
rules.note: Terminal O on S(VI), also sulfonate O-: sulfone O (OY).

rules.name: phosphoryl-O
rules.note: Terminal O on P: O= of dimethyl phosphate (O2).

rules.name: carbonyl-O
rules.note: C=O oxygen: ketone O (O).

rules.name: acid-OH-on-S-P
rules.note: OH of a sulfonic, sulfuric or phosphoric acid: carboxylic acid OH (OH).

rules.name: hydroxyl-O-on-C
rules.note: OH on carbon: alcohol O (OH).

rules.name: ester-O-on-P
rules.note: P-O-C and P-O-P: ester O of dimethyl phosphate (OS).

rules.name: ether-O
rules.note: C-O-C and S-O-C (sulfonate and sulfate esters): dialkyl ether O (OS).

rules.name: phosphorus-V
rules.note: Four-coordinate P(V) (phosphates, phosphonates, phosphoramides, thiophosphates): P of dimethyl phosphate (P).

rules.name: sulfide-S
rules.note: C-S-C: sulfide S (S).

rules.name: thiol-S
rules.note: C-SH: thiol S (SH).

rules.name: sp3-CH3
rules.note: sp3 C (not in a 3- or 4-ring): alkane C (CT).

rules.name: sp3-CH2
rules.note: sp3 C (not in a 3- or 4-ring): alkane C (CT).

rules.name: sp3-CH
rules.note: sp3 C (not in a 3- or 4-ring): alkane C (CT).

rules.name: sp3-C
rules.note: sp3 C (not in a 3- or 4-ring): alkane C (CT).

rules.name: aromatic-C-6ring
rules.note: Aromatic C of a 6-membered ring (not shared with a 5-ring): benzene C (CA).

rules.name: carbonyl-C
rules.note: C=O carbon (urea, carbamate, hydrazide, acyl groups): amide C (C).

rules.name: sulfonamide-N
rules.note: N on S(=O)2 without N/O neighbours (e.g. tertiary sulfonamide, sulfamide): secondary sulfonamide N (N).

rules.name: amide-N-H2
rules.note: N on C=O or C=S (ureas, carbamates, thioamides, thioureas) without N/O neighbours: amide N (N).

rules.name: amide-N-H1
rules.note: N on C=O or C=S (ureas, carbamates, thioamides, thioureas) without N/O neighbours: amide N (N).

rules.name: amide-N-H0
rules.note: N on C=O or C=S (ureas, carbamates, thioamides, thioureas) without N/O neighbours: amide N (N).

rules.name: amine-N-H2
rules.note: sp3 or aryl amine N without N/O/S/P neighbours: amine N (NT).

rules.name: amine-N-H1
rules.note: sp3 or aryl amine N without N/O/S/P neighbours: amine N (NT).

rules.name: amine-N-H0
rules.note: sp3 or aryl amine N without N/O/S/P neighbours: amine N (NT).

rules.name: ammonium-N-H3

rules.name: ammonium-N-H1

rules.name: ammonium-N-H0

rules.name: azine-N-6ring
rules.note: Pyridine-type aromatic N of a 6-membered ring (not shared with a 5-ring): pyridine N (NC).

rules.name: H-on-sp3-C

rules.name: H-on-aromatic-C

rules.name: H-on-ammonium-N

rules.name: H-on-amine-N
